newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ex-bar girl pleads not guilty in Manila sex case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-bar girl pleads not guilty in Manila sex case.

text.p: The Philippines' most famous bar girl and carrier of HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, pleaded not guilty on Wednesday to charges of child abuse for having sex with a minor who fathered her son.

Sarah Jane Salazar, who shocked the largely conservative Roman Catholic country by openly carrying on an affair with her young lover despite her illness, stood nervously as a court clerk read the charges against her.

"Not guilty," the 21-year-old Salazar said to each of four charges against her -- two counts of having sex with a minor and two counts of exposing the boy to HIV -- for which she faces up to 66 years in prison if convicted.
The boy, who was not in court, was 16 when they began their highly publicised affair last year despite the objections of the boy's mother, who filed the case against her Salazar.
"The proof of the sexual intercourse is the baby," judge Priscilla Mijares said after Salazar's lawyer argued there was no evidence of sex between the couple.
"Without intercourse, there will be no baby," the judge said.
Salazar's lover has tested negative for HIV. The results of blood tests on their month-old son are not yet known.
Salazar, a former bar girl and one of about 30,000 Filipinos with HIV, publicly declared in 1994 that she was infected.
Her story has been the subject of a popular film.
